relationships.subject: cAMP-PKA signaling
relationships.evidence_quote: Finally, inhibition of cAMP-PKA signaling alleviated allodynia and elevated KCC2 expression in DNP rats.

key_findings: Blocking spinal dorsal horn HCN channels with ZD7288 restores KCC2 expression and relieves diabetic neuropathic pain, an effect prevented by the KCC2 blocker DIOA.
Inhibiting cAMP-PKA signaling alleviates allodynia and elevates KCC2, placing cAMP-PKA-regulated HCN channels upstream of KCC2 loss and altered GABA levels.
